newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bourse rises, seen locked in tight range.
newsitem.headline: Polish bourse rises, seen locked in tight range.

text.p: Most Polish shares fell on Wednesday but gains by some heavyweights pushed the main index up and analysts saw the market flat in the next few sessions in the absence of fresh signals to draw new capital to the bourse.
The main market's WIG index rose 0.5 percent, to 13,725.6, and turnover rose 3.4 percent to 82.5 million zlotys ($29.5 million) on both markets as 45 issues fell, 19 rose and 19 were flat.

Analysts said the three-week horizontal trend was likely to continue as new issues were drawing cash away from the secondary market and few people wanted to sell stocks at current prices, nine percent lower than the October 9 high.
"We might have sessions of slight changes of the WIG index to the end of the week...(as) there is a lack of capital," said Czeslaw Pospieszynski, an analyst at Bank Gdanski brokerage.

Some analysts said the central bank's Tuesday statement it might raise interest rates next year, without specifying whether it meant real, nominal or market interest rates, was bringing some uncertainty to the bourse.
Some analysts said a downtrend could emerge, caused by year-end profit-taking and companies' low 1996 earnings.
Others said the market still had some upside potential and could soon test 14,000 points of WIG.
Polish brewer Zywiec soared 9.9 percent to 149.5 zlotys ($53) in a low 0.7-million-zloty ($0.3 million) turnover, with analysts saying the low turnover likely exaggerated the rise.
Mass privatisation NFI units rose two percent in 19.5-million-zloty trade ($7 million).
